reasons: Replies are not checked, so a wrong response can cause errors far from the cause.
No tests are visible for this file.
Some ids are not encoded in addresses, for example in fetchResearchDocuments.

terms.meaning: A shared function that sends requests to the server and handles common settings.
A specific web address on the server that answers one kind of request.
The part of a web address after a question mark that carries filter values.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the API layer
sections.what: Brings in the shared request helper and the scan synthesis reply type.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: fetchDashboard
sections.title: Fetching the home dashboard
sections.what: Gets the summary numbers for the home dashboard, optionally limited to one industry or sub-industry.
sections.why: Lets the home page show scoped numbers.
sections.watch_out: The industry and sub-industry values are inserted into the address as given.

sections.name: fetchProjects
sections.title: Fetching project lists
sections.what: Gets a list of projects, optionally narrowed by search settings.
sections.why: Used by list pages that show projects.
sections.watch_out: Only plain text settings are supported, so nested filter values are not sent.

sections.name: fetchIndustrySegments
sections.title: Fetching industry segments
sections.what: Gets the segment names and project counts for one industry.
sections.watch_out: The industry name is encoded in the address, which keeps it safe.

sections.name: fetchProject
sections.title: Fetching one project
sections.what: Gets the basic details of a single project.
sections.watch_out: The project id is placed in the address without encoding.

sections.name: fetchScanData
sections.title: Fetching scan data
sections.what: Gets the data behind the benchmark scan for an industry, optionally limited to certain ids.
sections.why: Feeds the scan deck and bubble charts.
sections.watch_out: A long id list makes a long address, which some servers may reject.

sections.name: fetchScanSynthesis
sections.title: Requesting scan synthesis
sections.what: Sends the selected scan items to the server and gets back generated summary text. The server holds the key, so the browser never sees it.
sections.why: The comment explains that a failed generation returns an error so the slide can show a retry option.
sections.watch_out: Setting force to true asks for a fresh result each time, which may cost more.

sections.name: fetchGlossary
sections.title: Fetching the glossary
sections.what: Gets glossary terms, optionally for one industry.

sections.name: fetchChangelog
sections.title: Fetching a project changelog
sections.what: Gets the change history for one project, with optional settings.
sections.why: Feeds the change history on project pages.

sections.name: fetchRecentChanges
sections.title: Fetching recent changes
sections.what: Gets the most recent changes across projects, with a limit and an optional industry.
sections.watch_out: The limit is turned into text and sent as is.

sections.name: triggerResearch
sections.title: Starting project research
sections.what: Asks the server to start research on one project, with an optional focus.
sections.why: Lets a user trigger new research.
sections.watch_out: Starting research may cost money or take time on the server side.

sections.name: fetchResearchStatus
sections.title: Checking research status
sections.what: Asks whether research on a project is still running or finished.

sections.name: fetchResearchDocuments
sections.title: Fetching research documents
sections.what: Gets the documents produced by project research, optionally for one job.
sections.watch_out: The job id is not encoded in the address, so unusual characters could break the request.

sections.name: fetchUpdates
sections.title: Fetching updates
sections.what: Gets a page of project updates, with limit, offset, and industry options.
sections.why: Feeds the updates feed with paging.

sections.name: createProjectUpdate
sections.title: Creating a project update
sections.what: Sends a new dated update about a project, with its source and optional link or locator.
sections.why: Lets users record news about a project.
sections.watch_out: The data is sent as given, so the server must check it.

sections.name: patchUpdateUrl
sections.title: Changing an update's link
sections.what: Changes or removes the web link of one project update.
sections.why: Lets users fix a broken or missing source link.

sections.name: fetchCompanies
sections.title: Fetching companies
sections.what: Gets the list of companies, optionally for one industry.

sections.name: fetchCompany
sections.title: Fetching one company
sections.what: Gets the details of a single company.
sections.watch_out: The company id is not encoded in the address.

sections.name: fetchCompanyProjects
sections.title: Fetching a company's projects
sections.what: Gets the projects linked to one company.

sections.name: createCompany
sections.title: Creating a company
sections.what: Sends the details of a new company to the server.
sections.watch_out: Required fields are only checked by the server, not here.

sections.name: addCompanySource
sections.title: Adding a company source
sections.what: Adds a web source that describes a company.
sections.why: Lets users attach evidence to a company.

sections.name: patchCompanySource
sections.title: Changing a company source
sections.what: Updates an existing company source, such as turning it on or off.

sections.name: deleteCompanySource
sections.title: Deleting a company source
sections.what: Removes one company source.
sections.watch_out: Deletion is final on the server, so the screen must confirm first.

sections.name: triggerDiscovery
sections.title: Starting company discovery
sections.what: Asks the server to search for new information, either for all companies or one company.
sections.watch_out: Discovery runs can be slow and may cost money.

sections.name: fetchDiscoveryStatus
sections.title: Checking discovery status
sections.what: Asks whether a discovery run is still going, optionally for one job.

sections.name: fetchDiscoveryHistory
sections.title: Fetching discovery history
sections.what: Gets the list of past discovery runs.

sections.name: fetchProjectCompanies
sections.title: Fetching companies linked to a project
sections.what: Gets the companies connected to one project.

sections.name: linkCompanyToProject
sections.title: Linking a company to a project
sections.what: Connects a company to a project with a role and optional confidence and source.
sections.why: Lets users record who is involved in a project.
sections.watch_out: Confidence is not checked for range here.

sections.name: fetchCompanyAliases
sections.title: Fetching company aliases
sections.what: Gets the other names a company is known by.

sections.name: addCompanyAlias
sections.title: Adding a company alias
sections.what: Adds another name for a company.
sections.why: Helps the app match the company across sources.
sections.watch_out: Duplicate aliases are handled by the server, not here.

sections.name: deleteCompanyAlias
sections.title: Deleting a company alias
sections.what: Removes one alias from a company.
sections.why: Lets users fix wrong alias names.

sections.name: patchCompany
sections.title: Changing a company
sections.what: Updates details of an existing company. Each field can be set to empty.
sections.watch_out: Empty values are sent as null, which the server must accept.

sections.name: fetchSources
sections.title: Fetching sources
sections.what: Gets the list of sources, optionally filtered by type, enabled state, or industry.
sections.watch_out: Filters with an undefined value are dropped, so an empty filter is ignored.

sections.name: createSource
sections.title: Creating a source
sections.what: Adds a new source with its name, type, address, and optional rating and category.
sections.watch_out: The id must be unique, which only the server can confirm.

sections.name: patchSource
sections.title: Changing a source
sections.what: Updates an existing source's details, including turning it on or off.

sections.name: fetchSourcePacks
sections.title: Fetching source packs
sections.what: Gets the ready-made bundles of sources, optionally for one industry.

sections.name: importSourcePack
sections.title: Importing a source pack
sections.what: Adds a ready-made source bundle to the app, optionally for one industry.
sections.why: Speeds up setting up an industry.
sections.watch_out: Importing the same pack twice may create duplicates unless the server prevents it.

sections.name: fetchCompanyPacks
sections.title: Fetching company packs
sections.what: Gets the ready-made bundles of companies, optionally for one industry.

sections.name: importCompanyPack
sections.title: Importing a company pack
sections.what: Adds a ready-made company bundle, optionally for one industry.
sections.why: Speeds up setting up an industry.
sections.watch_out: Same duplicate risk as source packs.

sections.name: fetchProjectSources
sections.title: Fetching sources for a project
sections.what: Gets the sources linked to one project.

sections.name: linkProjectSource
sections.title: Linking a source to a project
sections.what: Connects an existing source to a project.
sections.why: Lets users attach evidence to a project.

sections.name: fetchProviderStatus
sections.title: Checking provider status
sections.what: Asks the server which search and language model providers are set up and which models are chosen.
sections.why: Lets a debug screen show whether the server is ready.
sections.watch_out: The reply exposes model names, which is useful for debugging but not secret.

sections.name: fetchProjectMaturity
sections.title: Fetching project maturity
sections.what: Gets the maturity assessment of one project.

sections.name: researchProjectMaturity
sections.title: Requesting new maturity research
sections.what: Asks the server to research and update a project's maturity assessment.
sections.why: Lets users refresh a maturity score.
sections.watch_out: Like other research actions, it may cost money or take time.

summary: The main collection of functions the app uses to talk to the server, covering dashboards, projects, companies, sources, research, and maturity.
purpose: Gives every screen one place to request or change data, so addresses are not scattered through the code.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Grouping requests in one file keeps the server addresses in one place.
how: Each function builds a web address, sends a request through the shared request helper, and returns the parsed reply. Some functions add search settings to the address, and some send data in the request body.
inputs: Identifiers, filter values, and form data supplied by the screens that call these functions.
outputs: The parsed server reply for each request, or an error if the request fails.
risks: Replies are returned without checking their shape, so a server change can break screens quietly. Some ids are placed in addresses without encoding.
debug: Find the function for the failing screen, check its address in the network panel, and compare the response with the expected shape.
